standard: GDD rework v2 · 80+ researched scenarios · scorecard-passed
note: The freedom not to marry or have children; resisting the 'settle down' / 'still-unmarried' pressure (esp. on women); worth beyond marital status & looks (UNESCO 1.2, 3.2, 2.2, 5.2). New v2 build, the equity heart of Chapter 7 and the essential counterpoint to Choosing & Building (g53). Marriage and kids are one path, not the measure of a life. Five modes: the script & the choice (autonomy over your own life), not marrying (UN&RE, bust the 'still-unmarried' worth-questioning stigma, heaviest on women), childfree complete (the freedom not to have children; womanhood isn't motherhood), hold your ground (handling family & social pressure kindly but firmly; worth beyond status, looks and the marriage market incl. colourism), worth-beyond-status & reflection. No pressure in any direction; every path dignified; never shames those who do marry or have children early; even-handed (men feel a version too). Distress from family conflict or coercion routed to support; forced marriage to help (181, 1091, 112, Childline 1098). Builds on Equal & Confident (g50) and Equalize (g26). India: the marriage timeline, 'log kya kahenge', and the worth-questioning stigma fall sharpest on women.

evidenceBase: The default 'marry then have biological children' script is one valid path among many, not the measure of a life or a verdict on worth: people hold real autonomy over whether, when and whom to marry and whether to have children, and the right to a life of dignity includes the right to choose, including to choose differently, single, partnered, childfree, later, or queer. Increasingly, educated, financially independent adults choose these paths from a place of abundance and self-definition, not lack (UNESCO autonomy & challenging-norms; childfree-by-choice research)

The stigma falls hardest on women and is about social control, not truth: a woman's worth is never her marital status, and womanhood is not the same as motherhood, so being unmarried or childfree as one ages does not lower a person's value. The 'still unmarried?' and 'when are you having kids?' pressure, the 'log kya kahenge', and the marriage-market scrutiny (including colourism) are pressures to resist kindly but firmly, separating self-worth from marital and parental status and from looks (UNESCO gender equality; India childfree/single-women stigma research)

Every path is dignified and no one is shamed: the node applies no pressure in any direction and never shames those who do marry or have children, including early, it is even-handed (men feel a version of the 'settle down' pressure too, though it falls hardest on women), and it equips people to hold their ground with family without losing themselves or starting a family war. Distress from family conflict or coercion is routed to support, and forced marriage, which is never acceptable, to help (181, 1091, 112, Childline 1098) (autonomy & safeguarding practice)

myth.re: People genuinely want different lives; a meaningful life looks different for everyone.
myth.why: Diversity of wants is real, not a cover story.

scenarios.relearn: People genuinely want different lives; a meaningful life looks different for everyone.

scenarios.hook: Sort: builds worth that lasts, or worth the world can take away?

items.text: Your values and how you live

scenarios.relearn: Values, growth and relationships build worth that lasts; approval and market standing can be taken away.

scenarios.hook: You do want a partner eventually, but not on anyone else's timeline.

options.text: Wait for the right person and the right time, yours
options.consequence: You keep both the want and the autonomy.

options.text: Settle for anyone to meet the deadline
options.consequence: Waiting for the right person on your own timeline beats settling for anyone to meet a deadline.

scenarios.debrief: Wanting a partner and refusing to rush it aren't in conflict; the right time is yours to judge.
scenarios.relearn: Wait for the right person on your own timeline; don't settle to meet a deadline.

scenarios.hook: Match the truth to the path it frees.
scenarios.relearn: Worth-isn't-status, womanhood-isn't-motherhood and your-life-your-call each free a path.

scenarios.hook: Match the parenthood choice to its validity.
scenarios.relearn: One child, several, or none can all be right, for different people.

scenarios.hook: Family conflict over your choices is becoming genuinely distressing.

options.text: Reach for support, a counsellor or trusted person
options.consequence: You look after your wellbeing in the conflict.

options.text: Carry the distress entirely alone
options.consequence: Reaching for support (a counsellor or trusted person) helps when family conflict over your choices turns distressing.

scenarios.debrief: Sustained family conflict over life choices can be heavy; support helps you hold your ground and your wellbeing.
scenarios.relearn: If family conflict over your choices turns distressing, reach for support.

scenarios.hook: Sam: the bravest, kindest thing can be to live honestly as yourself, on your own path. Believe it?
scenarios.affirm: Living honestly as yourself, on your own path, is a quiet bravery that gives others permission too.
scenarios.relearn: Living honestly as yourself, on your own path, is brave and kind.

scenarios.hook: A young cousin says she feels worthless because she's 'still single'.
scenarios.setup: Reframe her worth for her. Say:

yourLine.text: "Your worth has nothing to do with being single, you're whole and valuable exactly as you are."
"Don't worry, we'll find you someone."

scenarios.relearn: Tell someone struggling that their worth has nothing to do with being single.

scenarios.hook: Sam: your path, your call, whichever path you choose, choose it freely and own it fully. Ready?
scenarios.affirm: Choose freely and own it fully, that's the whole heart of your path being your call.
scenarios.relearn: Whichever path you choose, choose it freely, own it fully, and respect everyone else's.
